components.meaning: woman
child

compositionNote: A woman (女) beside her child (子) — the ancient picture of all being good and well.
poem: A mother and her child,
together, reconciled —
when woman meets with son,
then GOOD (hǎo) has begun!

components.meaning: a person standing with arms and legs spread wide

compositionNote: An ancient picture of a person standing with arms flung wide, taking up as much space as possible — the very picture of 'big'.
poem: Arms flung wide, legs spread apart,
a stick-figure giant from the start.
Take up space, stand tall and proud —
BIG (dà) and mighty, big and loud!

components.meaning: three tiny dots, like grains of sand or specks of dust

compositionNote: A pictograph of tiny specks so small they could be swept up with one hand — hence 'small'.
poem: Three tiny grains, so small they fall,
swept aside, not big at all.
Pinch them close with finger and thumb —
SMALL (xiǎo) is what these three specks become.

components.meaning: evening (originally a piece of meat, 肉)
evening (originally a piece of meat, 肉)

compositionNote: Two pieces of meat (夕, originally 肉) stacked one on top of the other, showing a growing pile — hence 'many'.
poem: Two chunks of meat piled on a plate,
stacked up high, they simply can't wait.
Pile on more, don't hold it back —
MANY (duō) means plenty, stack on stack!

components.meaning: small
a stroke cutting away, showing something removed

compositionNote: One more small stroke is sliced away from 小 (small), leaving even less behind — so 少 means 'few'.
poem: Small (小) got a stroke sliced clean away,
less and less with each passing day.
What was little shrinks once more —
FEW (shǎo) is smaller than before.

meanings.def: to go up; to get on; to attend

components.meaning: a short mark placed above a horizontal baseline

compositionNote: An indicative symbol: a short stroke sits above a baseline (一), pointing straight at the idea of 'above'.
poem: A dash floats high above the ground,
pointing up without a sound.
Climb the ladder, rise, don't stall —
UP (shàng) and over, above it all.

meanings.def: to go down; to get off

components.meaning: a short mark placed below a horizontal baseline

compositionNote: An indicative symbol: a short stroke sits below a baseline (一), pointing straight at the idea of 'below'.
poem: A dash sinks low beneath the line,
dropping down, that's its design.
Gravity pulls, so let it fall —
DOWN (xià) and under, below it all.

components.meaning: a footprint, meaning to walk or advance (worn down to 䒑 at the top)
originally a boat (舟), now shaped like the moon radical
knife

compositionNote: Originally a foot (止) stepping onto a boat (舟, now written 月) with a knife (刀) cutting the mooring line — the picture of moving onward, hence 'front, before'.
poem: A foot steps down onto a boat,
knife cuts the rope, and off they float.
Sailing onward, leading the way —
FRONT (qián) is ahead, come what may.

components.meaning: a person, turned to represent a ruler
mouth, issuing a command

compositionNote: A ruler (人) gives orders with the mouth (口) — originally 'sovereign; queen', later borrowed as the simplified form meaning 'behind, after'.
poem: A ruler turns, his mouth commands,
issuing orders through the land.
But turn around, and there you'll see —
BEHIND (hòu) is where the queen will be.

components.meaning: field
earth; soil

compositionNote: A field (田) of earth (土) — originally a village where people farmed and lived, later coming to mean 'inside' and a measure of distance.
poem: A field of earth, soil dark and deep,
inside the village, safe to keep.
Step through the gate, come stay a while —
INSIDE (lǐ) this place, walk every mile.

components.meaning: evening
to divine (a crack pattern on an oracle bone)

compositionNote: Divining (卜) in the evening (夕), an unusual time to do it, was 'outside' normal custom — hence 外 means 'outside'.
poem: At dusk, a diviner cracks the bone,
reading signs from the great unknown.
Odd hour, place beyond the door —
OUTSIDE (wài) is what it stands for.

components.meaning: an enclosure or target
a vertical line piercing straight through

compositionNote: A line (丨) runs straight through the center of a shape (口), like an arrow hitting dead center on a target — hence 'middle'.
poem: An arrow flies and finds its mark,
straight through the center, hits the bark.
Not left, not right, but dead-on true —
MIDDLE (zhōng) is the aim that flew.

meanings.def: host; owner (in compounds like 房东, 股东)

components.meaning: tree (visible in the traditional form 東)
sun (visible in the traditional form 東)

compositionNote: The traditional form 東 showed the sun (日) rising up behind a tree (木) — the direction the sun comes from: east. The simplified 东 keeps only a trace of that picture.
poem: The sun climbs up behind a tree,
glowing bright for all to see.
Where morning light first starts to spring —
EAST (dōng) is that bright rising thing.

components.meaning: a bird settling into its nest at sunset

compositionNote: An ancient picture of a bird settling into its nest as the sun goes down — the direction of sunset is 'west'.
poem: A little bird flies home at last,
settling in as daylight's passed.
Where the sun dips low and mild —
WEST (xī) is dusk's returning child.

components.meaning: an ancient hanging bell-shaped instrument, faced south in ritual

compositionNote: An ancient picture of a hanging musical instrument, traditionally set facing the warm southern direction during rituals — giving 南 its meaning of 'south'.
poem: A hanging bell, ancient and grand,
faced the warmth of sunlit land.
Toward the heat, the bright, the wide —
SOUTH (nán) is that sunny side.

components.meaning: a person, reversed (facing away)
a person, reversed (facing away)

compositionNote: Two people stand back to back, facing away from each other — since houses traditionally faced south, the sunless, back-facing direction became 'north'.
poem: Two people stand back to back,
turned away from the sunny track.
Cold and shaded, dim the light —
NORTH (běi) is the chilly side of night.

components.meaning: one; a line representing what lies above
a person standing with arms outstretched

compositionNote: A line (一) drawn above a person (大) shows what is above a person's head — the sky, and by extension 'heaven' and 'day'.
poem: A line floats high above a man,
stretching over all the land.
Above his head, the blue does reign —
SKY (tiān) each day, and bright again.

components.meaning: grain; a ripe crop (seen in the original form)
person, carrying the harvest (seen in the original form)

compositionNote: Originally a picture of a person (人) carrying a bundle of ripe grain (禾) on their back — one harvest cycle marked a 'year'.
poem: A farmer bends beneath the load,
grain piled high along the road.
One harvest done, the seasons spin —
YEAR (nián) is a cycle wrapping in.

components.meaning: a crescent moon, seen hanging in the sky

compositionNote: A picture of a crescent moon — the character for 'moon', and since the moon's cycle marks roughly thirty days, also 'month'.
poem: A silver sliver curves up high,
a crescent hanging in the sky.
Each cycle marks a month within —
the MOON (yuè) is where new months begin.

components.meaning: a round sun with a mark at its center

compositionNote: A picture of the round sun with a dot at its heart — the character for 'sun', and since one sunrise marks one day, also 'day'.
poem: A circle glows with a dot at heart,
a burning sun, a fiery art.
It rises once to start the day —
SUN (rì) and day, both come this way.

components.meaning: a bright celestial body, like the sun
to grow; be born — used here for its sound (phonetic)

compositionNote: A bright object in the sky (日) combines with 生 (shēng), used here for its sound, to write 'star'.
poem: The sun (日) gave birth (生) to sparks of light,
scattered specks across the night.
Tiny, bright, and far away —
STARS (xīng) that twinkle till the day.

components.meaning: that; his/her/its — used here for its sound (phonetic)
moon, representing the passage of time

compositionNote: The moon (月) marks the passing of time, while 其 (qí) lends its sound — together forming 期, 'a period of time'.
poem: The moon (月) keeps count as it shows its face,
其 lends the sound that gives it grace.
Days and weeks in cycles spin —
a TERM (qī), a period locked within.

components.meaning: a lid or cover, coming together
something enclosed underneath the cover

compositionNote: A lid (亼) closes down over something and holds it close — the present moment, right now, hence 今 means 'now'.
poem: A lid comes down and seals it tight,
holding this moment, day or night.
Not past, not future, only here —
NOW (jīn) is the moment, always near.

components.meaning: sun
moon

compositionNote: The sun (日) by day and the moon (月) by night, the two brightest lights in the sky, combine to mean 'bright'.
poem: The sun (日) by day, the moon (月) by night,
together they make double bright.
Two lamps combined can never dim —
BRIGHT (míng) is the glow that comes from them.

components.meaning: sun; day
suddenly; just now — used here for its sound (phonetic)

compositionNote: The day (日) that has just passed — with 乍 lending its sound — gives 昨, 'yesterday'.
poem: The sun (日) that shone has since moved on,
sudden (乍) as the day is gone.
Look behind you, not so near —
YESTERDAY (zuó) is always here.

components.meaning: jade (玉), whose polished shine becomes visible
to see; to appear

compositionNote: Jade (王, from 玉) becomes visible to the eye (见) once polished — showing what appears right now, hence 现 means 'present; to appear'.
poem: Jade (玉) shines bright before the eye (见),
its hidden gleam no longer shy.
Right before us, plain to see —
NOW (xiàn) it shows, for you and me.

components.meaning: sun, marking the passage of time
temple — used here for its sound (phonetic)

compositionNote: The sun (日) tracks the passing hours, while 寺 lends its sound — together forming 时, 'time'.
poem: The sun (日) ticks by, a temple's (寺) bell,
counting hours it knows so well.
Hour by hour, the moments climb —
TIME (shí) is the sound of passing time.

components.meaning: person
marquis; nobleman — used here mainly for its sound (phonetic), with an extra stroke added

compositionNote: A person (亻) stands watching and waiting, with 侯 lending its sound — giving 候, 'to wait' and 'a period of time'.
poem: A person (亻) waits, a marquis's (侯) name,
watching, patient, just the same.
Standing still as moments pass —
WAIT (hòu), the time will come at last.

meanings.def: minute; a small fractional unit (money, score)

components.meaning: eight; here a picture of two strokes splitting apart
knife

compositionNote: A knife (刀) cuts something into two separate parts (八) — hence 分 means 'to divide', and by extension a small divided unit like a 'minute'.
poem: A knife (刀) comes down and cuts things two (八),
splitting parts from something new.
Break it down, share and spend —
DIVIDE (fēn), and minutes bend.

components.meaning: metal
middle — used here for its sound (phonetic)

compositionNote: A metal (钅) object with 中 lending its sound — giving 钟, a metal bell or clock.
poem: A metal (钅) bell rings dead center (中),
tolling hours as they enter.
Tick and chime, the sound rings true —
CLOCK (zhōng) is what it says to you.

components.meaning: to occupy — used here for its sound (phonetic)
fire, shown as four small flickering dots

compositionNote: A flickering flame (灬) with 占 lending its sound — together giving 点, a tiny bright 'dot', and by extension a 'point' in time.
poem: A flame (灬) flickers, small and bright,
占 lends its sound to catch the light.
Tiny spark upon the wall —
a DOT (diǎn), a point, an hour's call.

components.meaning: to divide; split apart
ox

compositionNote: An ox (牛) split (八) right down the middle — since oxen are large and easily divided, 半 came to mean 'half'.

words.meaning: half a day; a long while

poem: An ox (牛) is split (八) right down the seam,
divided evenly, it would seem.
Not whole, not none, just in between —
HALF (bàn) is the fairest share I've seen.

components.meaning: mountain-like shape, worn down from an original footstep 止
evening, echoing the passing of time

compositionNote: The traditional 歲 combined two footsteps marking the passage of time with an axe for its sound; the simplified 岁 keeps a mountain-like top (山) and 夕, still tracking each year that passes.
poem: A mountain step, an evening glow,
marking years as seasons go.
Each birthday climbed, a peak to gain —
YEARS OLD (suì) counted, again, again.

components.meaning: mouth, making a sound
a bent shape representing breath escaping — a cry or call

compositionNote: A mouth (口) lets out a cry (丂) — originally 'to call out', later used for a numbered mark, like the 'number' of a date.
poem: A mouth (口) lets out a bending cry (丂),
calling loud beneath the sky.
Give it digits, give it place —
NUMBER (hào) marks the date, the space.

meanings.def: to be called (name); to call out; to shout

components.meaning: mouth, making a sound
twisted cords — used here for its sound (phonetic)

compositionNote: A mouth (口) calls out loudly, with 丩 lending its sound — giving 叫, 'to call' or 'to shout'.

words.meaning: to be called; to be known as

poem: A mouth (口) shouts out, twisted (丩) and loud,
calling names out of the crowd.
Raise your voice, don't be shy —
CALL (jiào) it out, give it a try.

components.meaning: evening; dusk
mouth, calling out

compositionNote: At dusk (夕), when faces could no longer be seen, people called out with their mouths (口) to identify themselves — hence 名 means 'name'.
poem: At dusk (夕), no face is left to see,
so mouths (口) call out, "It's me, it's me!"
Spoken loud so all may know —
NAME (míng) is the word we call and show.
